verbatim_list: The unemployment rate of Saudi nationals was broadly unchanged at 6.5% in the second quarter of 2026.

Saudi employment increased by 34,000 in the quarter, but the employment of non-Saudis (excluding domestic workers) fell by 17,000. This was the first quarterly decline in non-Saudi employment since the fourth quarter of 2023.

Saudi employment increased by 11,325 workers in the construction sector, 9,271 in manufacturing, and 4,917 in retail and wholesale, while non-Saudi employment fell in these sectors by 68,743, 19,930, and 17,652, respectively.
Interestingly, there was some substitution of Saudi for non-Saudi labor within these sectors.
Labor market data, however, is a backward-looking indicator.
publisher: Arab Gulf States Institute in Washington (AGSI)
title: Saudi Labor Market Holds Firm in Face of Regional Conflict
key_claim: Non-Saudi employment (excluding domestic workers) fell by 17,000 in Q2 2026, the first quarterly decline since Q4 2023, driven by construction, while Saudi employment rose by 34,000.
frame_summary: Argues the Saudi labour market is bending but not breaking, and cautions that the data are a backward-looking indicator.
